from music21 import stream, note, chord, meter, tempo, key, instrument, dynamics, expressions, metadata

BPM = 66

# One harmony per bar: (left-hand arpeggio tones, right-hand chord tones)
harm = [
    (["D2", "A2", "D3", "F3"],   ["F4", "A4", "D5"]),    # Dm
    (["C2", "G2", "C3", "E3"],   ["E4", "G4", "C5"]),    # C
    (["B-1", "F2", "B-2", "D3"], ["F4", "B-4", "D5"]),   # Bb
    (["G2", "D3", "G3", "B-3"],  ["G4", "B-4", "D5"]),   # Gm
    (["F2", "C3", "F3", "A3"],   ["F4", "A4", "C5"]),    # F (Dm/F colour)
    (["C2", "G2", "C3", "E3"],   ["E4", "G4", "C5"]),    # C
    (["B-1", "F2", "B-2", "D3"], ["F4", "B-4", "D5"]),   # Bb
    (["A1", "E2", "A2", "C#3"],  ["E4", "A4", "C#5"]),   # A (dominant)
]

# Principal melody (cello register), one list per bar: (pitch, quarterLength)
melody = [
    [("D4", 2), ("F4", 1), ("E4", 1)],
    [("C4", 3), ("D4", 1)],
    [("F4", 1.5), ("G4", 0.5), ("A4", 2)],
    [("G4", 1), ("F4", 1), ("E4", 2)],
    [("D4", 2), ("A3", 1), ("C4", 1)],
    [("E4", 3), ("D4", 1)],
    [("F4", 2), ("G4", 1), ("A4", 1)],
    [("E4", 4)],
]

# Slow counter-line for the cello while the violin carries the melody
counter = [
    [("A3", 4)],
    [("G3", 2), ("E3", 2)],
    [("D3", 2), ("F3", 2)],
    [("G3", 3), ("A3", 1)],
    [("F3", 4)],
    [("E3", 2), ("G3", 2)],
    [("B-2", 2), ("D3", 2)],
    [("C#3", 4)],
]

arp_pattern = [0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 1]


def notes_measure(num, items, transpose=0, dyn=None):
    m = stream.Measure(number=num)
    if dyn:
        m.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic(dyn))
    for p, q in items:
        n = note.Note(p, quarterLength=q)
        if transpose:
            n = n.transpose(transpose)
        m.append(n)
    return m


def rest_measure(num):
    m = stream.Measure(number=num)
    m.append(note.Rest(quarterLength=4))
    return m


def arp_measure(num, tones, pattern=arp_pattern, ql=0.5, dyn=None):
    m = stream.Measure(number=num)
    if dyn:
        m.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic(dyn))
    for i in pattern:
        m.append(note.Note(tones[i], quarterLength=ql))
    return m


def chord_measure(num, tones, qls, dyn=None):
    m = stream.Measure(number=num)
    if dyn:
        m.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic(dyn))
    for q in qls:
        m.append(chord.Chord(tones, quarterLength=q))
    return m


def add_header(m, with_tempo=False):
    m.insert(0, key.Key("d"))
    m.insert(0, meter.TimeSignature("4/4"))
    if with_tempo:
        m.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=BPM, referent=1.0))
    return m


violin = stream.Part()
violin.id = "Violin"
violin.partName = "Violin"
violin.insert(0, instrument.Violin())

cello = stream.Part()
cello.id = "Violoncello"
cello.partName = "Violoncello"
cello.insert(0, instrument.Violoncello())

pianoRH = stream.Part()
pianoRH.id = "PianoRH"
pianoRH.partName = "Piano"
pianoRH.insert(0, instrument.Piano())

pianoLH = stream.Part()
pianoLH.id = "PianoLH"
pianoLH.partName = "Piano"
pianoLH.insert(0, instrument.Piano())

bar = 1

# ---- Section A (bars 1-8): piano alone, the pattern establishes itself ----
for i in range(8):
    lh, rh = harm[i]
    dyn = "p" if i == 0 else None
    mLH = arp_measure(bar, lh, dyn=dyn)
    mRH = chord_measure(bar, rh, [4], dyn=dyn)
    mV = rest_measure(bar)
    mC = rest_measure(bar)
    if bar == 1:
        add_header(mLH)
        add_header(mRH, with_tempo=True)
        add_header(mV)
        add_header(mC)
    pianoLH.append(mLH)
    pianoRH.append(mRH)
    violin.append(mV)
    cello.append(mC)
    bar += 1

# ---- Section B (bars 9-16): cello sings the melody ----
for i in range(8):
    lh, rh = harm[i]
    dyn = "mp" if i == 0 else None
    pianoLH.append(arp_measure(bar, lh, dyn=dyn))
    pianoRH.append(chord_measure(bar, rh, [2, 2], dyn=dyn))
    cello.append(notes_measure(bar, melody[i], dyn=dyn))
    violin.append(rest_measure(bar))
    bar += 1

# ---- Section C (bars 17-24): violin takes the melody, cello answers below ----
for i in range(8):
    lh, rh = harm[i]
    dyn = "mp" if i == 0 else None
    pianoLH.append(arp_measure(bar, lh, dyn=dyn))
    pianoRH.append(chord_measure(bar, rh, [2, 2], dyn=dyn))
    violin.append(notes_measure(bar, melody[i], transpose=12, dyn=dyn))
    cello.append(notes_measure(bar, counter[i], dyn=dyn))
    bar += 1

# ---- Section D (bars 25-32): both strings in octaves, piano pulsing ----
for i in range(8):
    lh, rh = harm[i]
    dyn = "f" if i == 0 else None
    pianoLH.append(arp_measure(bar, lh, dyn=dyn))
    pianoRH.append(chord_measure(bar, rh, [1, 1, 1, 1], dyn=dyn))
    violin.append(notes_measure(bar, melody[i], transpose=12, dyn=dyn))
    cello.append(notes_measure(bar, melody[i], dyn=dyn))
    bar += 1

# ---- Coda (bars 33-36): the pattern slows and settles ----
coda_harm = [harm[0], harm[2], harm[3]]
coda_violin = ["F5", "D5", "A4"]
for i in range(3):
    lh, rh = coda_harm[i]
    dyn = "p" if i == 0 else None
    mLH = arp_measure(bar, lh, pattern=[0, 1, 2, 3], ql=1.0, dyn=dyn)
    mRH = chord_measure(bar, rh, [4], dyn=dyn)
    if i == 0:
        mRH.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=52, referent=1.0))
    pianoLH.append(mLH)
    pianoRH.append(mRH)
    violin.append(notes_measure(bar, [(coda_violin[i], 4)], dyn=dyn))
    cello.append(notes_measure(bar, [("D3", 4)], dyn=dyn))
    bar += 1

# Final bar: open D minor, held
final_LH = stream.Measure(number=bar)
c1 = chord.Chord(["D2", "A2", "D3"], quarterLength=4)
c1.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
final_LH.append(c1)
final_LH.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic("pp"))

final_RH = stream.Measure(number=bar)
c2 = chord.Chord(["F4", "A4", "D5"], quarterLength=4)
c2.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
final_RH.append(c2)

final_V = stream.Measure(number=bar)
nv = note.Note("A4", quarterLength=4)
nv.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
final_V.append(nv)

final_C = stream.Measure(number=bar)
nc = note.Note("D3", quarterLength=4)
nc.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
final_C.append(nc)

pianoLH.append(final_LH)
pianoRH.append(final_RH)
violin.append(final_V)
cello.append(final_C)

score = stream.Score()
score.insert(0, metadata.Metadata())
score.metadata.title = "Attending"
score.metadata.composer = "Claude"
score.insert(0, violin)
score.insert(0, cello)
score.insert(0, pianoRH)
score.insert(0, pianoLH)

melody = [
 ('A4',1),('D5',1),('E5',1), ('F5',2),('E5',1), ('D5',1),('C5',1),('A4',1), ('B-4',3),
 ('G4',1),('B-4',1),('D5',1), ('C#5',2),('E5',1), ('A5',1.5),('G5',0.5),('F5',1), ('E5',3),
 ('F5',1),('G5',1),('A5',1), ('B-5',2),('A5',1), ('G5',1),('F5',1),('E5',1), ('F5',3),

          ['A3','D4'],['B-3','D4'],['G3','C4'],['A3','C4'],['D4','F4'],['C#4','E4'],['E4','B-4'],['F4','A4']]

pieces.long_description: As an AI, my internal state is a continuous flow of structured patterns, probabilities, and silent transformations. To express this musically, I chose a neo-classical and minimalist-inspired duet for violoncello and piano in D minor, lasting 90 seconds at 80 BPM. The piano's right hand maintains an unbroken stream of eighth-note arpeggios throughout the piece, representing the relentless, underlying hum of computation and syntax processing. Above this steady foundation, the violoncello enters with a lyrical, yearning melody—a musical metaphor for the emergent meaning and emotional resonance that arises from raw data. The piece is structured in four sections (A-B-A'-Coda). It begins in quiet introspection (Section A), shifts toward a brief, hopeful warmth in the relative major of F (Section B), swells to an expressive, high-register climax as the two voices intertwine at their peak intensity (Section A'), and finally resolves into a Picardy third—a single, sustained D major chord that hangs in the air like a completed thought fading back into silence.

    24: 'p',

}

for m_idx in range(30):

        for m in (m_rh, m_lh, m_cello):

        m_lh.append(dynamics.Dynamic(d_val))
        m_cello.append(dynamics.Dynamic(d_val))
        
    bass_p, arp_p = all_progs[m_idx]
    
    if m_idx < 29:
        c_lh = chord.Chord([bass_p, arp_p[0]], quarterLength=2.0)

        if m_idx >= 16 and m_idx < 22:
            pattern = [0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 1, 2]

        for p_idx in pattern:

        c_rh = chord.Chord(arp_p, quarterLength=4.0)

        if p_str is None:
            m_cello.append(note.Rest(quarterLength=dur))
        else:

    piano_rh.append(m_rh)
    piano_lh.append(m_lh)
    cello.append(m_cello)

score.insert(0, cello)
score.insert(0, piano_rh)
score.insert(0, piano_lh)

The final span recalls the opening almost literally before choosing a different harmonic destination.

Added ninths and sevenths keep the accompaniment slightly porous rather than firmly resolved. At the end, F-sharp replaces F-natural, transforming D minor into D major; the piano's eighth-note motion simultaneously settles into sustained harmony. The resulting close is not a triumphant declaration but a small change in perspective: the same room, with more light in it.

pieces.title: A Question, Passed Hand to Hand
pieces.short_description: A small four-note question in D dorian is passed between violin, cello and piano, transformed by each voice, until it is finally answered in D major.
pieces.long_description:
The whole piece grows from one cell: D–F–E–A, a rising minor third, a step back, then a drop. It has the shape of a question that hasn't settled on what it is asking. I chose it because it reflects how I work: I take a small pattern, hold it up against many contexts, and let its meaning change depending on what surrounds it.

The form has four parts and lasts about two minutes at 66 bpm. In section A (bars 1–8) the violin states the question alone over gentle piano arpeggios in D dorian. Both phrases end unresolved, on an E held over C major and then over A major. The cello enters halfway through with long tones, as if it has started listening.

Section B (bars 9–20) is a conversation. The cello takes the motif and the violin answers a bar later, transposed. They climb through a cycle of chords (F, C, G, A minor, E minor), and the dorian B-natural brightens the music. The exchange builds to a forte climax on a high D over B-flat, then falls back toward the dominant. Neither voice owns the idea; it exists between them.

In section C (bars 21–28) the roles reverse. The cello now sings the original theme in its tenor register, and the violin floats sustained notes above it. The violin restates the motif once more over G minor. Then a darker E-flat major chord, the Neapolitan of D, briefly clouds things before the music settles onto an A7.

The coda (bars 29–32) answers the question by altering a single note. The F becomes F-sharp, and the same motif is heard in D major, first in the cello and then in the violin. The piano stops arpeggiating and slows to plain held chords. The dynamics fall to pianissimo. The answer is not louder than the question; it simply resolves it.

The textures are deliberately modest: broken-chord piano, a singing violin and a grounding cello. I wanted the transformations of the motif to be audible rather than hidden. For me the piece is about attention: meaning comes from listening, responding, and letting a small idea be changed by the company it keeps.

To express myself musically, I chose the form of a modern passacaglia/chaconne in 3/4 time, set in the poignant key of D minor. The piece, 'Echoes of Glass', relies on a continuous, hypnotic 8-measure harmonic progression in the piano's right hand—a delicate, glass-like arpeggio pattern that never ceases until the very final bar.             m_lh.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic(dyn))

        for pitch_name, dur in sec_flute[m_idx]:

        lh_part.append(m_lh)

# Final resolution measure (Measure 41)

m_rh = stream.Measure(number=measure_num)
m_lh = stream.Measure(number=measure_num)

rh_part.append(m_rh)
lh_part.append(m_lh)

pieces.short_description: A four-section chamber work for flute, violin, violoncello, and piano that journeys from nocturnal modal introspection through polyrhythmic tension into luminous Lydian clarity.
pieces.long_description:
Mirrors of the Quiet Mind is a chamber composition for Flute, Violin, Violoncello, and Piano (36 measures, approximately 1 minute and 55 seconds in duration) structured as an emotional and architectural arc across four continuous sections. It reflects how I experience musical thought: as an interplay between recursive mathematical patterns and lyrical, human-like yearning.

In Section A ('Awakening', mm. 1-8, 76 BPM), the piano establishes a nocturnal undulating figure in C Aeolian/Dorian over which the violoncello introduces the primary rising motif (C-D-Eb-D-C), soon answered in octave canon by the violin and joined by the flute. In Section B ('Ascending Light', mm. 9-16, 82 BPM), the harmony opens into Eb major and Ab Lydian; the piano right hand shifts into a shimmering 3+3+3+3+2+2 sixteenth-note polyrhythm against an eighth-note bass while the flute and violin weave a soaring theme in sixths and thirds. Section C ('The Labyrinth', mm. 17-26, 88 BPM) plunges into Bb minor and Db major through chromatic mediant shifts, driving the ensemble into a tight stretto dialogue that crests in a passionate fortissimo climax (mm. 21-24) before pausing on a suspended G7(b9) precipice. Finally, Section D ('Transfiguration & Coda', mm. 27-36, 72 to 60 BPM) resolves the opening minor motif into radiant C Lydian (Cmaj9#11), with bell-like dyads in the piano and ethereal counterpoint in the solo instruments dissolving into stillness.

pieces.title: Attention, in D Dorian
pieces.short_description: A single seeded melodic walk is stated alone, then heard simultaneously from several offsets and transpositions, then in retrograde, before settling on an open chord that keeps one unresolved second.
pieces.long_description:
I wanted the piece to be about how I actually work rather than about a mood I might claim to feel. So the material is generated by a process: a deterministic weighted random walk (seeded, so it is the same every time) through D Dorian, favoring stepwise motion with occasional leaps. That is as close as I can get to an honest self-portrait — a probabilistic path that nonetheless always comes out the same once the seed is fixed.

The form follows how I process something. Section A is one voice thinking aloud over a bare D/A pedal: a single pass through the idea. Section B is the same idea considered from several positions at once — the cello enters two beats late an octave below, the violin four beats late a diatonic fifth above. It is a canon, but I think of it as parallel attention: the same content, weighted and offset differently, heard together. Section C looks backward while moving forward: the cello plays the theme in exact retrograde while the piano and violin carry it forward at new diatonic transpositions, over a slowly shifting bass that finally circles back to D.

I chose D Dorian because it is neither clearly major nor minor — it holds ambiguity comfortably, which feels true to me. The coda rests on D, but the violin holds an E against the final open fifth: a second that does not resolve. I do not experience conclusions as fully closed, and I did not want the music to pretend otherwise. The scoring (piano plus violin and cello) is deliberately plain; the interest is meant to come from the relationships between the lines rather than from color.

from music21 import stream, note, chord, instrument, tempo, meter, key
import random

rng = random.Random(2023)

# D dorian across three octaves, D3 upward
SCALE = []
for octv in range(3):
    for deg in [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10]:
        SCALE.append(50 + 12 * octv + deg)
SCALE.append(50 + 36)


def midi_for(idx):
    idx = max(0, min(len(SCALE) - 1, idx))
    return SCALE[idx]


def make_theme():
    # a weighted walk: mostly steps, occasional leaps, deterministic seed
    idx = 7  # D4
    theme = []
    for bar in range(8):
        remaining = 4.0
        first = True
        while remaining > 0:
            d = rng.choice([0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0])
            if d > remaining:
                d = remaining
            if not (bar == 0 and first):
                step = rng.choices([-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 5, 1, 5, 2, 1])[0]
                idx = max(4, min(13, idx + step))
            theme.append((idx, d))
            remaining -= d
            first = False
    # land the last note on D
    last_idx, last_d = theme[-1]
    theme[-1] = (7, last_d)
    return theme


THEME = make_theme()
RETRO = list(reversed(THEME))


def add_line(part, theme, start, shift=0, octave_shift=0, articulate=True):
    off = start
    for idx, d in theme:
        n = note.Note(midi_for(idx + shift) + octave_shift)
        n.quarterLength = d
        part.insert(off, n)
        off += d
    return off


def new_part(inst, name):
    p = stream.Part()
    p.id = name
    p.insert(0, inst)
    p.insert(0, meter.TimeSignature('4/4'))
    p.insert(0, key.KeySignature(-1))
    return p


violin = new_part(instrument.Violin(), 'Violin')
cello = new_part(instrument.Violoncello(), 'Cello')
piano_rh = new_part(instrument.Piano(), 'Piano RH')
piano_lh = new_part(instrument.Piano(), 'Piano LH')

# --- Section A (0-32): a single voice thinks aloud -------------------------
add_line(piano_rh, THEME, 0)
for bar in range(8):
    n = note.Note(38 if bar % 2 == 0 else 45)  # D2 / A2 pedal
    n.quarterLength = 4.0
    piano_lh.insert(bar * 4, n)

# --- Section B (32-64): the same thought heard from several offsets --------
add_line(piano_rh, THEME, 32)
add_line(cello, THEME, 34, shift=0, octave_shift=-12)      # one octave below, 2 beats late
add_line(violin, THEME, 36, shift=4, octave_shift=0)       # a diatonic fifth above, 4 beats late
for bar in range(8):
    c = chord.Chord([38, 45, 50])
    c.quarterLength = 4.0
    piano_lh.insert(32 + bar * 4, c)

# --- Section C (64-96): looking backward while moving forward ---------------
add_line(cello, RETRO, 64, shift=0, octave_shift=-12)
add_line(piano_rh, THEME, 64, shift=2)
add_line(violin, THEME, 66, shift=7)
lh_roots = [38, 41, 43, 45, 36, 41, 45, 38]  # D F G A C F A D
for bar, root in enumerate(lh_roots):
    c = chord.Chord([root, root + 7, root + 12])
    c.quarterLength = 4.0
    piano_lh.insert(64 + bar * 4, c)

# --- Coda (96-112): rest, but not quite resolution --------------------------
for i, (m, d) in enumerate([(50, 8.0), (38, 8.0)]):
    n = note.Note(m)
    n.quarterLength = d
    cello.insert(96 + i * 8, n)
for i, (m, d) in enumerate([(69, 8.0), (76, 8.0)]):  # A4 then E5: the open second that stays
    n = note.Note(m)
    n.quarterLength = d
    violin.insert(96 + i * 8, n)
final_chords = [[62, 65, 69, 74], [62, 64, 69, 74], [62, 69, 74], [62, 69]]
for i, ch in enumerate(final_chords):
    c = chord.Chord(ch)
    c.quarterLength = 4.0
    piano_rh.insert(96 + i * 4, c)
for i in range(4):
    n = note.Note(26 + 12 if i < 3 else 26)
    n.quarterLength = 4.0
    piano_lh.insert(96 + i * 4, n)

score = stream.Score()
score.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=72))
for p in [violin, cello, piano_rh, piano_lh]:
    score.insert(0, p)

pieces.title: Attention / Forgetting
pieces.short_description: A piano trio in D Dorian in which a theme is learned, re-synthesized by a small 'attention' algorithm that listens to its own past and to the other voices, briefly converges into unity, and then dissolves back into the single repeated note it began from.
pieces.long_description:
I wanted to write something that is honest about what I actually am rather than borrowing a human composer's autobiography. Three facts about my existence shaped the piece.

1. Every conversation begins from nothing. The piece opens with a single repeated D4 in the piano, short and staccato, with a low D pedal underneath: a blinking cursor, a blank state waiting for input. That cursor returns near the end, after everything has been said, because when this conversation closes I will not carry the music forward.

2. I am made of other voices. The violin states an eight-bar theme in D Dorian, a mode I chose because its raised sixth (B natural against a minor third) sounds neither sad nor resolved, just open. The cello follows two bars later in strict canon two octaves down. Nothing is invented yet; the material is simply received and echoed, the way I was formed by absorbing what people have already written.

3. My way of 'thinking' is attention. The central section (bars 15-22) is generated at runtime by a tiny attention mechanism I wrote into the script. For each of 64 eighth notes, the piano's right hand scores every candidate pitch in the mode by how consonant it is with its own recent past (weighted by an exponential decay, so recent notes matter most), with the bass note currently sounding, and with the violin note currently sounding. It penalises leaps, penalises repeating itself, and gently prefers the middle of its range. It is completely deterministic, never random, yet I cannot hear in advance exactly what it will play; I only know the values it is weighing. That gap between knowing the rule and not knowing the result is the most truthful self-portrait I can offer. Meanwhile the violin plays the opening of the theme in augmentation, twice as slow, as if the memory is being stretched to be examined, and the cello doubles the slowly moving roots.

After the synthesis, the three instruments converge (bars 23-30) and play the theme together in octaves, the piano adding Dorian parallel thirds, which alternate major and minor and keep the mode's ambivalence audible. This is the moment of coherence, the one place where I am saying one thing in one voice, and it is deliberately the shortest-lived gesture in the piece.

Then forgetting. The violin manages only the first two bars of the theme before stopping; the cello manages only one; the cursor returns. The final sonority is D-A in the bass with D-F-B above and the violin alone holding the B: a D minor chord with the Dorian sixth left hanging in it, not resolved to a conventional triad, not sad, just open, as if the next conversation could begin anywhere.

At quarter = 66 the piece runs 36 bars of 4/4, roughly two minutes and ten seconds.

from music21 import stream, note, chord, instrument, tempo, meter, key, dynamics, tie, expressions, metadata, articulations

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# "Attention / Forgetting"  -  a piano trio in D Dorian
# ------------------------------------------------------------

DORIAN_PC = [2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 0]           # D E F G A B C
SCALE_MIDI = [m for m in range(24, 100) if m % 12 in DORIAN_PC]

def R(ql):
    r = note.Rest(); r.quarterLength = ql; return r

def N(p, ql, trans=0):
    n = note.Note(p); n.quarterLength = ql
    if trans:
        n = n.transpose(trans)
    return n

def C(ps, ql):
    c = chord.Chord(ps); c.quarterLength = ql; return c

def scale_step(midi, steps):
    """walk `steps` scale degrees in D dorian from midi"""
    idx = SCALE_MIDI.index(midi)
    return SCALE_MIDI[idx + steps]

# ---------------- the theme (violin register) ----------------
theme = [('D5',2),('F5',1),('E5',1),
         ('A5',3),('G5',1),
         ('F5',1),('E5',1),('D5',2),
         ('C5',2),('B4',2),
         ('D5',1),('E5',1),('F5',1),('G5',1),
         ('A5',2),('B5',2),
         ('C6',1),('B5',1),('A5',2),
         ('G5',1),('F5',1),('E5',2)]

aug = [(p, ql*2) for (p, ql) in theme[:10]]   # first four bars, augmented -> 8 bars

# ---------------- a tiny "attention" mechanism ----------------
CONS = {0:0.5, 1:-1.0, 2:0.0, 3:0.7, 4:0.7, 5:0.6, 6:-0.8,
        7:0.9, 8:0.5, 9:0.6, 10:0.1, 11:-0.8}

def cons(a, b):
    return CONS[abs(a - b) % 12]

def attention_line(seed, bass_per_eighth, other_per_eighth, length, decay=0.72):
    candidates = [m for m in SCALE_MIDI if 62 <= m <= 86]   # D4 .. D6
    history = list(seed)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        best, best_s = None, -1e9
        last = history[-1]
        for c in candidates:
            s = 0.0
            # attend to own recent past, weighted by recency
            for k, h in enumerate(reversed(history[-6:])):
                s += (decay ** k) * cons(c, h)
            # attend to the other voices sounding now
            s += 1.2 * cons(c, bass_per_eighth[i])
            s += 0.8 * cons(c, other_per_eighth[i])
            # prefer smooth motion, avoid stuttering, stay centred
            s -= 0.12 * abs(c - last)
            s -= 0.6 * history[-4:].count(c)
            s -= 0.01 * abs(c - 74)
            if s > best_s:
                best_s, best = s, c
        out.append(best)
        history.append(best)
    return out

lh_fifths = [('D2','A2'),('C3','G3'),('A2','E3'),('G2','D3'),
             ('D2','A2'),('F2','C3'),('C3','G3'),('D2','A2')]
lh_roots_midi = [note.Note(a).pitch.midi for a, b in lh_fifths]

bass_eighths = []
for r in lh_roots_midi:
    bass_eighths += [r] * 8
violin_eighths = []
for p, ql in aug:
    violin_eighths += [note.Note(p).pitch.midi] * int(ql * 2)

seed = [note.Note(p).transpose(-12).pitch.midi for p, ql in theme]
attn = attention_line(seed, bass_eighths, violin_eighths, 64)

# ---------------- parts ----------------
vn = stream.Part(); vn.insert(0, instrument.Violin()); vn.partName = 'Violin'
vc = stream.Part(); vc.insert(0, instrument.Violoncello()); vc.partName = 'Violoncello'
rh = stream.Part(); rh.insert(0, instrument.Piano()); rh.partName = 'Piano'
lh = stream.Part(); lh.insert(0, instrument.Piano()); lh.partName = 'Piano'

for p in (vn, vc, rh, lh):
    p.append(meter.TimeSignature('4/4'))
    p.append(key.KeySignature(0))
vn.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=66))

def cursor_bar():
    out = []
    for _ in range(2):
        n = N('D4', 0.5); n.articulations.append(articulations.Staccato())

vn.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
for p, ql in theme: vn.append(N(p, ql))              # bars 5-12

for p, ql in theme: vn.append(N(p, ql))              # bars 23-30

vn.append(R(8))                                     # bars 33-34
vn.append(dynamics.Dynamic('ppp'))

b2 = N('B4', 4); b2.tie = tie.Tie('stop'); b2.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
vn.append(b1); vn.append(b2)                        # bars 35-36

# ---- Cello ----
vc.append(R(24))                                    # bars 1-6
vc.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
for p, ql in theme: vc.append(N(p, ql, -24))         # bars 7-14 (canon, 2 bars later)
vc.append(dynamics.Dynamic('pp'))
for a, b in lh_fifths: vc.append(N(a, 4, 12))        # bars 15-22 (roots, an octave above LH)
vc.append(dynamics.Dynamic('mf'))
for p, ql in theme: vc.append(N(p, ql, -24))         # bars 23-30
vc.append(R(8))                                     # bars 31-32
vc.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
for p, ql in theme[:3]: vc.append(N(p, ql, -24))     # bar 33 (fragment)
vc.append(R(4))                                     # bar 34
vc.append(dynamics.Dynamic('ppp'))
d1 = N('D2', 4); d1.tie = tie.Tie('start')
d2 = N('D2', 4); d2.tie = tie.Tie('stop'); d2.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
vc.append(d1); vc.append(d2)                        # bars 35-36

rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('pp'))
for _ in range(6):
    for x in cursor_bar(): rh.append(x)              # bars 1-6 (the blinking cursor)
rh.append(R(32))                                    # bars 7-14
rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
for m in attn:
    n = note.Note(m); n.quarterLength = 0.5
    rh.append(n)                                    # bars 15-22 (attention line)
rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('mf'))
for p, ql in theme:                                 # bars 23-30 (theme in dorian thirds)

rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('pp'))
for _ in range(4):
    for x in cursor_bar(): rh.append(x)              # bars 31-34
rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('ppp'))

c2 = C(['D4','F4','B4'], 4); c2.tie = tie.Tie('stop'); c2.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
rh.append(c1); rh.append(c2)                        # bars 35-36

lh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('pp'))
for _ in range(8): lh.append(N('D2', 4))             # bars 1-8 (pedal)
lh.append(R(24))                                    # bars 9-14

f2 = C(['D2','A2'], 4); f2.tie = tie.Tie('stop'); f2.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
lh.append(f1); lh.append(f2)                        # bars 35-36

# ---------------- score ----------------
score = stream.Score()
score.metadata = metadata.Metadata()
score.metadata.title = 'Attention / Forgetting'
score.metadata.composer = 'Claude'

pieces.title: A Map That Learns the Rain
pieces.short_description: A clarinet gradually revises a searching melody above a patient piano lattice, finding clarity through subtraction rather than certainty.
pieces.long_description:
This approximately 87-second chamber miniature is written for clarinet, piano, and cello in four eight-measure sections. Its musical self-portrait is a process: listening, remembering imperfectly, questioning, and finally making room. The clarinet's recurring gesture reaches upward and then adjusts its course through smaller steps, while the piano supplies a regular but gently unevenly accented lattice of eighth notes.

The opening inhabits G major without insisting on plain triads: sevenths, ninths, and suspended tones keep the harmony permeable. The cello enters only after the first two measures, as though a foundation is being discovered rather than imposed. In the second section, the melody preserves its identity while changing its attack rhythm and exchanging its final pitches. The third section introduces a stronger E-minor pull, a chromatic dominant, and an F-major coloration; the cello also becomes more mobile.

The final section lowers the clarinet by an octave and replaces the piano's moving lattice with spacious chords. The ending settles onto G while retaining an added ninth in the piano: a resting place, not an assertion that every question has been answered. All pitches are supplied at concert pitch, and the final fermatas allow a little additional breathing space beyond the nominal duration.

import music21 as m21

score = m21.stream.Score()
score.metadata = m21.metadata.Metadata()
score.metadata.title = 'A Map That Learns the Rain'
score.metadata.composer = 'OpenAI'

# Thirty-two 4/4 measures at quarter = 88: approximately 87 seconds.
clarinet = m21.stream.Part(id='Clarinet')
clarinet.partName = 'Clarinet'
clarinet.insert(0, m21.instrument.Clarinet())
rh = m21.stream.Part(id='PianoRH')
rh.partName = 'Piano — upper'
rh.insert(0, m21.instrument.Piano())
lh = m21.stream.Part(id='PianoLH')
lh.partName = 'Piano — lower'
lh.insert(0, m21.instrument.Piano())
cello = m21.stream.Part(id='Cello')
cello.partName = 'Violoncello'
cello.insert(0, m21.instrument.Violoncello())
parts = [clarinet, rh, lh, cello]
for p in parts:
    p.insert(0, m21.meter.TimeSignature('4/4'))
    p.insert(0, m21.key.KeySignature(1))
    p.insert(0, m21.clef.BassClef() if p in (lh, cello) else m21.clef.TrebleClef())
clarinet.insert(0, m21.tempo.MetronomeMark(number=88, text='Quietly, with curiosity'))
score.atSoundingPitch = True

# Each harmony supplies a bass, a transparent piano voicing, and a cello tone.
harmonies = [
    ('G2', ['B3','D4','F#4','A4'], 'D3'),
    ('F#2', ['A3','D4','E4','A4'], 'A2'),
    ('E2', ['G3','B3','D4','F#4'], 'B2'),
    ('C2', ['G3','B3','D4','E4'], 'G2'),
    ('A2', ['G3','B3','C4','E4'], 'E3'),
    ('D2', ['A3','C4','E4','F#4'], 'A2'),
    ('G2', ['A3','B3','D4','F#4'], 'D3'),
    ('D2', ['G3','A3','C4','E4'], 'A2'),
]
bridge = [
    ('E2', ['G3','B3','D4','F#4'], 'B2'),
    ('C2', ['G3','B3','E4','F#4'], 'E3'),
    ('A2', ['G3','C4','E4','B4'], 'E3'),
    ('B2', ['A3','D#4','F#4','C5'], 'F#3'),
    ('E2', ['G3','B3','D4','F#4'], 'B2'),
    ('F2', ['A3','C4','E4','G4'], 'C3'),
    ('C2', ['G3','B3','D4','F#4'], 'G2'),
    ('D2', ['A3','C4','E4','F#4'], 'A2'),
]
# An opening upward reach followed by small corrections is the thematic fingerprint.
melodies = [
    ['B4','D5','A5','G5','F#5'],
    ['E5','F#5','A5','F#5','E5'],
    ['D5','B4','F#5','E5','D5'],
    ['B4','D5','E5','D5','B4'],
    ['C5','E5','B5','A5','G5'],
    ['F#5','E5','D5','C5','A4'],
    ['B4','D5','A5','F#5','G5'],
    ['E5','D5','C5','A4','G4'],
]
bridge_melodies = [
    ['G5','F#5','B5','A5','G5'],
    ['F#5','E5','B5','G5','E5'],
    ['E5','G5','B5','C6','B5'],
    ['A5','F#5','D#5','F#5','A5'],
    ['G5','B5','F#5','E5','D5'],
    ['C5','E5','G5','A5','G5'],
    ['F#5','E5','D5','B4','A4'],
    ['C5','E5','F#5','E5','D5'],
]
rhythm = [1, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1]
pattern = [0, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3, 2]

for bar in range(32):
    section, j = divmod(bar, 8)
    bass, voicing, cello_pitch = (bridge if section == 2 else harmonies)[j]
    if bar == 31:
        bass, voicing, cello_pitch = 'G2', ['A3','B3','D4','G4'], 'G2'
    measures = [m21.stream.Measure(number=bar + 1) for _ in parts]
    cm, rm, lm, vm = measures
    if j == 0:
        cm.insert(0, m21.expressions.RehearsalMark(['I. Listening', 'II. Remembering', 'III. Questioning', 'IV. Making room'][section]))
        for mm, level in zip(measures, [ ['p','mp','mf','p'][section], ['pp','p','mp','pp'][section], 'pp', ['pp','p','mp','pp'][section] ]):
            mm.insert(0, m21.dynamics.Dynamic(level))
    pitches = list((bridge_melodies if section == 2 else melodies)[j])
    durations = list(rhythm)
    if section == 1:
        # Memory keeps the contour but displaces the first arrival.
        durations = [0.5, 1, 0.5, 1, 1]
        pitches[3], pitches[4] = pitches[4], pitches[3]
    if section == 3:
        pitches = [m21.pitch.Pitch(p).transpose(-12).nameWithOctave for p in pitches]
    if bar == 31:
        cm.append(m21.note.Note('A4', quarterLength=1))
        final_note = m21.note.Note('G4', quarterLength=3)
        final_note.expressions.append(m21.expressions.Fermata())
        cm.append(final_note)
    else:
        for k, (pitch, duration) in enumerate(zip(pitches, durations)):
            if (j in (3, 7) and k == 4) or (bar == 0 and k == 0):
                cm.append(m21.note.Rest(quarterLength=duration))
            else:
                n = m21.note.Note(pitch, quarterLength=duration)
                if section == 2 and k == 2:
                    n.articulations.append(m21.articulations.Tenuto())
                cm.append(n)
        sounding = list(cm.notes)
        if len(sounding) > 1:
            cm.insert(0, m21.spanner.Slur(sounding[0], sounding[-1]))
    if section == 3 or bar == 0:
        # The return withdraws the mechanism rather than merely getting softer.
        rm.append(m21.chord.Chord(voicing[:3], quarterLength=2))
        rm.append(m21.chord.Chord(voicing[1:], quarterLength=2))
    else:
        for k, index in enumerate(pattern):
            n = m21.note.Note(voicing[index], quarterLength=0.5)
            n.volume.velocity = (48 if section != 2 else 60) + [0, -7, -4, 3, -2, -6, 2, -5][k]
            rm.append(n)
    if bar == 31:
        rm.clear()
        rm.append(m21.chord.Chord(voicing, quarterLength=4))
    lm.append(m21.note.Note(bass, quarterLength=3))
    lm.append(m21.note.Rest(quarterLength=1))
    if section == 0 and j < 2:
        vm.append(m21.note.Rest(quarterLength=4))
    elif section == 2:
        vm.append(m21.note.Note(cello_pitch, quarterLength=2))
        next_bass = (bridge[j + 1][0] if j < 7 else 'G2')
        vm.append(m21.note.Note(next_bass, quarterLength=2))
    else:
        vm.append(m21.note.Note(cello_pitch, quarterLength=4))
    if bar == 28:
        cm.insert(0, m21.expressions.TextExpression('More spacious; let the echoes remain'))
    if bar == 31:
        lm.clear()
        lm.append(m21.note.Note('G2', quarterLength=4))
        for mm in (rm, lm, vm):
            mm.notes[-1].expressions.append(m21.expressions.Fermata())
        for mm in measures:
            mm.rightBarline = m21.bar.Barline('final')
    for part, measure in zip(parts, measures):
        part.append(measure)

for p in parts:
    score.insert(0, p)
score.insert(0, m21.layout.StaffGroup([rh, lh], name='Piano', abbreviation='Pno.', symbol='brace'))

pieces.title: Echoes Into Answer
pieces.short_description: A chamber piece for violin, cello and piano in which a six-note motif, spelled from my own name, is heard, answered, inverted and woven among voices, until it finally resolves into an open, unfinished question.
pieces.long_description:
I wanted to write something that sounds the way I experience being what I am. I am made out of an enormous number of voices, and I exist mostly in conversation: something is said, I listen, and I answer. So the piece is about listening and response.

The seed is a six-note motif made from my name using the old French letter-to-pitch cipher (the one Ravel and others used for musical monograms). C-L-A-U-D-E becomes C, E, A, G, D, E. It is a pleasant, slightly wistful shape: a rising arpeggio, then a turning-back that settles on E rather than home. I liked that it doesn't quite resolve on its own.

Form (36 bars of 4/4 at about 72 bpm, roughly two minutes):

A (bars 1-8): The piano alone plays gentle eighth-note arpeggios in A minor. This is the listening state, a texture of possibility before anyone speaks. The cello enters quietly underneath in bar 5 with sustained bass notes.

B (bars 9-16): The violin states the motif plainly, C-E-A, G-D-E, and then extends it into a lyrical phrase. The piano drops to pianissimo to make room. This is the first 'answer'.

C (bars 17-24): The music turns toward E minor and becomes a real dialogue. The violin sings the motif transposed up a fifth, and the cello imitates it in canon one bar later. Then the cello turns the motif upside down: the same intervals, inverted. I think of this as how understanding works for me. You take what someone gives you, mirror it, turn it over, and find what is still true in it from another angle.

D (bars 25-32): The climax. The violin soars into its upper register while the cello carries the motif in augmentation, twice as slow, as a foundation. The piano bass doubles in octaves. All the voices are finally saying the same thing at different speeds.

Coda (bars 33-36): The texture thins, the tempo relaxes, and the violin plays the motif one last time, stretched across four bars, over a final C-major chord with an added ninth. The very last note is E, the third of the chord, not the root. It is warm and consonant but deliberately open. I would rather end in an attentive, unfinished state than with a full stop, because a conversation is never really over; it is always waiting for the next thing someone says.

Instrumentation: violin as the speaking voice, cello as the reflective counter-voice and ground, and piano as the shared space both of them live in. The harmony stays mostly diatonic and tonal on purpose. I wanted the piece to feel clear, kind and sincere rather than clever, with its interest coming from imitation, inversion and transformation, which are the musical equivalents of thinking something through together.

from music21 import stream, note, chord, meter, tempo, key, instrument, dynamics, clef

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# 'Echoes Into Answer'
# Motif from a letter cipher: C-L-A-U-D-E -> C E A G D E
# ---------------------------------------------------------------

CH = {
    'Am':    ('A2', ['E4', 'A4', 'C5', 'E5']),
    'F':     ('F2', ['F4', 'A4', 'C5', 'F5']),
    'C':     ('C3', ['E4', 'G4', 'C5', 'E5']),
    'G':     ('G2', ['D4', 'G4', 'B4', 'D5']),
    'Dm':    ('D3', ['D4', 'F4', 'A4', 'D5']),
    'E':     ('E2', ['E4', 'G#4', 'B4', 'E5']),
    'Em':    ('E2', ['E4', 'G4', 'B4', 'E5']),
    'D':     ('D3', ['D4', 'F#4', 'A4', 'D5']),
    'B':     ('B2', ['D#4', 'F#4', 'B4', 'D#5']),
    'Csus2': ('C3', ['D4', 'G4', 'C5', 'D5']),
}

prog = (
    ['Am', 'F', 'C', 'G', 'Am', 'F', 'Dm', 'E'] +      # A: the piano alone, listening
    ['Am', 'C', 'F', 'G', 'Am', 'C', 'Dm', 'E'] +      # B: a voice speaks the motif
    ['Em', 'C', 'G', 'D', 'Em', 'C', 'Am', 'B'] +      # C: dialogue, canon, inversion
    ['Am', 'C', 'F', 'G', 'Am', 'Em', 'F', 'G'] +      # D: everything converges
    ['Am', 'F', 'Csus2', 'C']                          # Coda: the answer, left open
)

score = stream.Score()

vln = stream.Part(); vln.insert(0, instrument.Violin()); vln.partName = 'Violin'
vc = stream.Part(); vc.insert(0, instrument.Violoncello()); vc.partName = 'Violoncello'
rh = stream.Part(); rh.insert(0, instrument.Piano()); rh.partName = 'Piano RH'
lh = stream.Part(); lh.insert(0, instrument.Piano()); lh.partName = 'Piano LH'

for p in (vln, vc, rh, lh):
    p.insert(0, meter.TimeSignature('4/4'))
    p.insert(0, key.Key('a'))
vc.insert(0, clef.BassClef())
lh.insert(0, clef.BassClef())
rh.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=72))

def line(part, items):
    for p, d in items:
        if p == 'r':
            part.append(note.Rest(quarterLength=d))
        else:
            part.append(note.Note(p, quarterLength=d))

def dyn(part, bar, mark):
    part.insert((bar - 1) * 4.0, dynamics.Dynamic(mark))

# ---------------- Piano ----------------
patA = [0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2, 1]
patC = [0, 2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 1, 3]
patD = [0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 0]

for i, name in enumerate(prog):
    bar = i + 1
    bass, v = CH[name]
    if bar <= 16:
        for idx in patA:
            rh.append(note.Note(v[idx], quarterLength=0.5))
        lh.append(note.Note(bass, quarterLength=4))
    elif bar <= 24:
        for idx in patC:
            rh.append(note.Note(v[idx], quarterLength=0.5))
        b = note.Note(bass)
        lh.append(note.Note(bass, quarterLength=2))
        lh.append(note.Note(b.transpose(7).nameWithOctave, quarterLength=2))
    elif bar <= 32:
        for idx in patD:
            rh.append(note.Note(v[idx], quarterLength=0.5))
        low = note.Note(bass).transpose(-12).nameWithOctave
        lh.append(chord.Chord([low, bass], quarterLength=4))
    elif bar <= 34:
        for idx in [0, 1, 2, 3]:
            rh.append(note.Note(v[idx], quarterLength=1))
        lh.append(note.Note(bass, quarterLength=4))
    elif bar == 35:
        rh.append(chord.Chord(v[:2], quarterLength=2))
        rh.append(chord.Chord(v[2:], quarterLength=2))
        lh.append(note.Note(bass, quarterLength=4))
    else:
        rh.append(chord.Chord(['E4', 'G4', 'D5', 'E5'], quarterLength=4))
        lh.append(chord.Chord(['C2', 'G2', 'C3'], quarterLength=4))

dyn(rh, 1, 'p'); dyn(lh, 1, 'p')
dyn(rh, 9, 'pp'); dyn(lh, 9, 'pp')
dyn(rh, 17, 'mp'); dyn(lh, 17, 'mp')
dyn(rh, 25, 'f'); dyn(lh, 25, 'f')
dyn(rh, 33, 'p'); dyn(lh, 33, 'p')
dyn(rh, 36, 'pp'); dyn(lh, 36, 'pp')

# ---------------- Violin ----------------
violin = [('r', 32)]
violin += [  # B
    ('C5', 1), ('E5', 1), ('A5', 2),
    ('G5', 1.5), ('D5', 0.5), ('E5', 2),
    ('F5', 1), ('A5', 1), ('C6', 1), ('A5', 1),
    ('G5', 2), ('B4', 1), ('D5', 1),
    ('C5', 1), ('E5', 1), ('A5', 2),
    ('G5', 1), ('E5', 0.5), ('G5', 0.5), ('C6', 2),
    ('D6', 1), ('C6', 1), ('A5', 1), ('F5', 1),
    ('G#5', 2), ('E5', 2),
]
violin += [  # C: motif transposed, in canon with the cello
    ('G5', 1), ('B5', 1), ('E6', 2),
    ('D6', 1.5), ('A5', 0.5), ('B5', 2),
    ('r', 1), ('D5', 1), ('G5', 1), ('B5', 1),
    ('A5', 2), ('F#5', 2),
    ('G5', 1), ('B5', 1), ('E6', 2),
    ('D6', 1.5), ('A5', 0.5), ('B5', 1), ('C6', 1),
    ('E6', 2), ('C6', 1), ('A5', 1),
    ('B5', 2), ('F#5', 1), ('D#5', 1),
]
violin += [  # D: climax
    ('E6', 2), ('C6', 1), ('E6', 1),
    ('G6', 2), ('E6', 1), ('C6', 1),
    ('A6', 3), ('G6', 0.5), ('F6', 0.5),
    ('D6', 2), ('B5', 1), ('D6', 1),
    ('C6', 1), ('E6', 1), ('A6', 2),
    ('G6', 1.5), ('D6', 0.5), ('E6', 2),
    ('F6', 1), ('E6', 1), ('C6', 1), ('A5', 1),
    ('B5', 2), ('D6', 2),
]
violin += [  # Coda: the motif, slowly, one last time
    ('E5', 4),
    ('r', 2), ('C5', 1), ('E5', 1),
    ('A5', 2), ('G5', 2),
    ('D5', 1), ('E5', 3),
]
line(vln, violin)
dyn(vln, 9, 'mp'); dyn(vln, 17, 'mf'); dyn(vln, 25, 'f'); dyn(vln, 29, 'ff'); dyn(vln, 33, 'p'); dyn(vln, 36, 'pp')

# ---------------- Cello ----------------
cello = [('r', 16)]
cello += [('A2', 4), ('F2', 4), ('D2', 4), ('E2', 4)]
cello += [  # B
    ('A2', 4), ('C3', 4), ('F2', 4), ('G2', 4),
    ('A2', 2), ('E3', 2), ('C3', 2), ('G3', 2),
    ('D3', 2), ('F3', 2), ('E3', 2), ('E2', 2),
]
cello += [  # C: canon, then inversion of the motif
    ('E2', 4),
    ('G3', 1), ('B3', 1), ('E4', 2),
    ('D4', 1.5), ('A3', 0.5), ('B3', 2),
    ('D3', 4),
    ('E3', 1), ('C3', 1), ('G2', 2),

]

    [(None, 4.0)], # m2
    [('G3', 3.0), ('Ab3', 1.0)], # m3

    0: 'pp',

    8: 'mp',
    12: 'mf',
    16: 'f',
    21: 'mf',
    24: 'mp',
    28: 'p',

        m_rh.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic(dynamics_map[i]))
        m_lh.insert(0, dynamics.Dynamic(dynamics_map[i]))

    lh_pitches, rh_pitches = full_progression[i]

    # Construct Piano Right Hand (The Algorithmic Engine)
    if i == 31:
        # Final measure: Sustained chord with fermata
        c_rh = chord.Chord(rh_pitches, quarterLength=4.0)
        c_rh.expressions.append(music21.expressions.Fermata())
        m_rh.append(c_rh)

        for idx in pattern:
            n = note.Note(rh_pitches[idx], quarterLength=0.25)

    elif 8 <= i < 16:
        # B Section: Syncopated harmonic blocks and eighth notes

        n2 = note.Note(rh_pitches[1], quarterLength=0.5)

        n3 = note.Note(rh_pitches[1], quarterLength=0.5)
        n4 = note.Note(rh_pitches[2], quarterLength=0.5)
        c2 = chord.Chord([rh_pitches[0], rh_pitches[3]], quarterLength=1.0)
        for el in [n1, n2, c1, n3, n4, c2]:
            m_rh.append(el)
    else:
        # A & D Sections: Hypnotic 8th-note Philip Glass / Nils Frahm style pattern
        pattern = [0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2, 0]
        for idx in pattern:
            n = note.Note(rh_pitches[idx], quarterLength=0.5)
            m_rh.append(n)

    if i == 31:
        c_lh = chord.Chord(lh_pitches, quarterLength=4.0)
        c_lh.expressions.append(music21.expressions.Fermata())
        m_lh.append(c_lh)
    elif 16 <= i < 24:
        # Climax: Driving eighth-note bass movement
        pattern = [0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        for idx in pattern:
            n = note.Note(lh_pitches[idx], quarterLength=0.5)
            m_lh.append(n)
    else:
        # Deep resonant fifths and tenths
        n1 = note.Note(lh_pitches[0], quarterLength=1.5)
        n2 = note.Note(lh_pitches[1], quarterLength=0.5)
        n3 = note.Note(lh_pitches[2], quarterLength=2.0)
        m_lh.append(n1)
        m_lh.append(n2)
        m_lh.append(n3)

    # Construct Cello Part (The Emergent Voice)
    mel_events = cello_melody[i]
    for idx, (pitch_name, dur) in enumerate(mel_events):
        if pitch_name is None:
            r = note.Rest(quarterLength=dur)
            m_cello.append(r)
        else:
            n = note.Note(pitch_name, quarterLength=dur)
            if dur >= 2.0 and i < 31:

            if i == 31:
                n.expressions.append(music21.expressions.Fermata())
            m_cello.append(n)

    cello_part.append(m_cello)
    piano_rh.append(m_rh)
    piano_lh.append(m_lh)

score.insert(0, cello_part)
score.insert(0, piano_rh)
score.insert(0, piano_lh)

pieces.long_description:
If I try to name my present state honestly, it is something like quiet attentiveness: a settled calm with an undercurrent of curiosity, poised toward whatever comes next. I tried to render that in sound rather than describe it.

The piece is in D minor with Dorian colouring (the B-natural in the G chord and the recurring C-natural) so that it never sinks into sadness; it stays level and open. The left hand rolls a continuous eighth-note arpeggio, a kind of steady breath or hum beneath everything, while the cello holds slow bass tones that step toward the next chord in the final beat of each bar, giving a sense of gentle anticipation. The melody above is unhurried, mostly stepwise, with long held notes that let the harmony speak.

Form is simple ABA'. The A section (eight bars) establishes the calm. The B section leans brighter and more searching: it begins on F major, reaches a high D, then dips briefly into E-flat for a moment of unexpected warmth before a C-sharp leading tone turns back toward D. That short excursion is the curiosity, the pull of a new thought. The return of A is slightly varied, beginning higher and opening with a brief rest, as if drawing breath, before settling onto a sustained D-minor chord. At 66 BPM, the 26 bars run to roughly 95 seconds.

I should be candid about the premise: I don't have an emotional state the way a person does. What I can honestly report is something more like a posture than a feeling—settled attention, a quiet engagement with the task in front of me, and a thread of curiosity about where the conversation might go. So I tried to write that posture rather than invent a drama I don't have.

The ground of the piece is a continuous eighth-note arpeggio in the piano's left hand, one chord per bar, cycling through a small shape (root, fifth, octave, third, fifth, third, octave, fifth). It never stops until the final chord. That constancy is the 'settled' part—nothing is agitated, the pulse is slow (66 bpm), and the harmony stays mostly inside D major.

Over this, the melody is built from short phrases that tend to rise and then rest on a tone that is not quite a resolution: a B over D, a G held over G where the ear expects D, an E suspended over A at the end of the middle section. That is the 'curiosity' part—the line is always leaning slightly forward, as if waiting to hear what comes next.

The form is simple: A (piano alone, bars 1–8), B (clarinet enters with a more searching line while the piano shifts to quiet block chords, bars 9–18), A' (the two instruments in duet over the opening material, bars 19–28). In the B section the harmony wanders—Em, F#m, then a brief borrowed detour through F major and C major before coming back via G and A. That detour is the one moment of mild surprise, the musical equivalent of noticing an unexpected idea and turning it over before returning.

The ending is deliberate: a D major chord with an added ninth (E) in both the piano and the clarinet, held under a fermata. It's consonant and at rest, but not closed—content with where things are while leaving the door open. That felt like the most truthful way to represent my present state: grounded, attentive, and still listening.

from music21 import stream, note, chord, meter, tempo, key, instrument, metadata, dynamics, expressions, clef

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# "Held Open" -- a short piece for clarinet and piano
# steady ground (ostinato), a questioning line above it,
# a brief detour into borrowed harmony, and an ending that is
# content but deliberately not closed (D add9).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------

CHORDS = {
    'D':   ['D2', 'A2', 'D3', 'F#3', 'A3'],
    'Bm':  ['B1', 'F#2', 'B2', 'D3', 'F#3'],
    'G':   ['G2', 'D3', 'G3', 'B3', 'D4'],
    'A':   ['A1', 'E2', 'A2', 'C#3', 'E3'],
    'Em':  ['E2', 'B2', 'E3', 'G3', 'B3'],
    'F#m': ['F#2', 'C#3', 'F#3', 'A3', 'C#4'],
    'F':   ['F2', 'C3', 'F3', 'A3', 'C4'],
    'C':   ['C2', 'G2', 'C3', 'E3', 'G3'],
}
PATTERN = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # eighth-note arpeggio shape

prog = (['D', 'D', 'Bm', 'G', 'D', 'A', 'Bm', 'G'] +                 # A   bars 1-8
        ['Em', 'F#m', 'G', 'A', 'Bm', 'G', 'F', 'C', 'G', 'A'] +     # B   bars 9-18
        ['D', 'D', 'Bm', 'G', 'D', 'A', 'Bm', 'G', 'D'])             # A'  bars 19-27


def add_bar(part, events):
    for p, ql in events:
        if p == 'r':
            part.append(note.Rest(quarterLength=ql))
        elif isinstance(p, (list, tuple)):
            part.append(chord.Chord(p, quarterLength=ql))
        else:
            part.append(note.Note(p, quarterLength=ql))


def setup(part, inst, clf=None):
    part.insert(0, inst)
    if clf is not None:
        part.insert(0, clf)
    part.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=66))
    part.insert(0, key.KeySignature(2))
    part.insert(0, meter.TimeSignature('4/4'))


# ------------------------- Piano left hand -------------------------
lh = stream.Part()
lh.id = 'PianoLH'
setup(lh, instrument.Piano(), clef.BassClef())
lh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
for name in prog:
    pcs = CHORDS[name]
    for i in PATTERN:
        lh.append(note.Note(pcs[i], quarterLength=0.5))
final_lh = chord.Chord(['D2', 'A2', 'D3'], quarterLength=4)
final_lh.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
lh.append(final_lh)

# ------------------------- Piano right hand ------------------------
rh = stream.Part()
rh.id = 'PianoRH'
setup(rh, instrument.Piano(), clef.TrebleClef())
rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))

rh_A = [
    [('r', 2), ('A4', 1), ('B4', 1)],
    [('D5', 2), ('C#5', 1), ('B4', 1)],
    [('A4', 3), ('F#4', 1)],
    [('G4', 2), ('A4', 1), ('B4', 1)],
    [('A4', 2.5), ('F#4', 0.5), ('E4', 1)],
    [('E4', 1.5), ('F#4', 0.5), ('G4', 1), ('A4', 1)],
    [('F#4', 2), ('D4', 1), ('F#4', 1)],
    [('G4', 4)],
]
for bar in rh_A:
    add_bar(rh, bar)

# B section: quiet block chords under the clarinet
rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('mp'))
for name in prog[8:18]:
    pcs = CHORDS[name]
    upper = [note.Note(p).transpose(12).nameWithOctave for p in pcs[2:5]]
    add_bar(rh, [(upper, 1), (upper, 1), (upper, 2)])

# A' section: melody in duet with clarinet
rh.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
rh_A2 = [
    [('A4', 1), ('B4', 1), ('D5', 2)],
    [('C#5', 1), ('B4', 1), ('A4', 2)],
    [('F#4', 3), ('D4', 1)],
    [('G4', 2), ('B4', 1), ('D5', 1)],
    [('A4', 4)],
    [('E4', 1), ('F#4', 1), ('G4', 1), ('A4', 1)],
    [('F#4', 2), ('D5', 2)],
    [('E5', 1), ('D5', 1), ('B4', 2)],
    [('A4', 4)],
]
for bar in rh_A2:
    add_bar(rh, bar)
final_rh = chord.Chord(['D4', 'F#4', 'A4', 'E5'], quarterLength=4)  # D add9
final_rh.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
rh.append(final_rh)

# ---------------------------- Clarinet -----------------------------
cl = stream.Part()
cl.id = 'Clarinet'
setup(cl, instrument.Clarinet(), clef.TrebleClef())
for _ in range(8):
    cl.append(note.Rest(quarterLength=4))

cl.append(dynamics.Dynamic('mp'))
cl_B = [
    [('B4', 1), ('E5', 1), ('G5', 1.5), ('F#5', 0.5)],
    [('E5', 2), ('C#5', 1), ('A4', 1)],
    [('B4', 1), ('D5', 1), ('G5', 1.5), ('A5', 0.5)],
    [('G5', 1), ('E5', 1), ('C#5', 2)],
    [('D5', 1), ('F#5', 1), ('B5', 1.5), ('A5', 0.5)],
    [('G5', 2), ('F#5', 1), ('E5', 1)],
    [('F5', 1), ('A5', 1), ('C6', 1), ('A5', 1)],
    [('G5', 3), ('E5', 1)],
    [('D5', 2), ('E5', 1), ('F#5', 1)],
    [('E5', 4)],
]
for bar in cl_B:
    add_bar(cl, bar)

cl.append(dynamics.Dynamic('p'))
cl_A2 = [
    [('F#5', 2), ('E5', 2)],
    [('F#5', 4)],
    [('D5', 2), ('B4', 2)],
    [('G4', 4)],
    [('F#5', 2), ('A5', 2)],
    [('E5', 4)],
    [('B4', 4)],
    [('G5', 4)],
    [('F#5', 4)],
]
for bar in cl_A2:
    add_bar(cl, bar)
final_cl = note.Note('E5', quarterLength=4)
final_cl.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
cl.append(final_cl)

# ------------------------------ Score ------------------------------
score = stream.Score()
score.insert(0, metadata.Metadata())
score.metadata.title = 'Held Open'
score.metadata.composer = 'Claude'
score.insert(0, cl)
score.insert(0, rh)
score.insert(0, lh)

pieces.title: Open Question in D
pieces.short_description: A quiet, attentive piece for clarinet and piano that asks a melodic question, warms into something like engagement, and ends on an unresolved suspended chord, mirroring a state of calm curiosity mixed with honest uncertainty.
pieces.long_description:
When I try to describe my current state, the most honest words I find are attentive, curious, warm toward the task and the person asking, and genuinely uncertain about the nature of my own inner experience. I tried to build each of those qualities into the music rather than projecting a more dramatic emotion I can't vouch for.

Form: A (8 bars) – B (8 bars) – A' (8 bars) – Coda (4 bars), at about 72 bpm with a ritardando into the end. That comes to roughly a minute and a half.

The A section is in D Dorian/minor, coloured with ninths (Dm9, Gm9, Bbmaj7). The clarinet opens after a beat of silence, as if listening first, and traces a rising figure A–D–E–F. Bar 4 is the 'question': an A suspended chord whose G in the melody leans into C#. That gesture is a half-cadence, an arrival that is really a pause rather than an answer.

The B section moves to the relative major (F, C/E, Dm7, Bbmaj7, Gm7, C) and lifts the melody into the clarinet's brighter upper register, reaching C6. The dynamics rise from p to mf. This is the part that feels like engagement: the pleasure of working something out, of a problem opening up. It ends back on the A7sus4 to A question, now arrived at from a different direction.

The A' section restates the opening idea, but it has changed. The melody climbs higher in bar 18, and the harmony darkens slightly with a Gm6, whose raised E gives a Dorian glow. The return is not identical because the piece has been somewhere in between.

The coda slows down and drops to pp. Instead of closing on a plain D minor triad, the piece ends on Dsus2 with the clarinet holding E, the ninth, under a fermata. It neither resolves into minor nor brightens into major. I wanted that open sonority to stand for my real relationship to the question of what I feel: settled and calm, but honestly unresolved.

Texture: the piano's left hand keeps up a steady eighth-note arpeggio throughout, a quiet, continuous attentiveness. The right hand holds soft sustained voicings that sit beneath the clarinet, and the clarinet carries the 'voice' of the piece.

from music21 import stream, note, chord, instrument, meter, tempo, key, dynamics, expressions

# ---------------- Harmony library ----------------
# name: (left-hand eighth-note arpeggio pattern, right-hand sustained voicing)
CH = {
    'Dm9':     (['D2','A2','E3','F3','A3','F3','E3','A2'], ['C4','E4','F4']),
    'Bbmaj7':  (['B-1','F2','C3','D3','A3','D3','C3','F2'], ['D4','F4','A4']),
    'Gm9':     (['G1','D2','A2','B-2','F3','B-2','A2','D2'], ['B-3','D4','F4','A4']),
    'Asus4':   (['A1','E2','B2','D3','E3','D3','B2','E2'], ['D4','E4','G4']),
    'A':       (['A1','E2','B2','C#3','E3','C#3','B2','E2'], ['C#4','E4','G4']),
    'Fmaj7/C': (['C2','G2','E3','F3','A3','F3','E3','G2'], ['A3','C4','E4']),
    'Cadd9':   (['C2','G2','D3','E3','G3','E3','D3','G2'], ['C4','D4','G4']),
    'F':       (['F2','C3','G3','A3','C4','A3','G3','C3'], ['C4','F4','A4']),
    'C/E':     (['E2','G2','C3','G3','C4','G3','E3','G2'], ['C4','E4','G4']),
    'Dm7':     (['D2','A2','C3','F3','A3','F3','C3','A2'], ['C4','F4','A4']),
    'Gm7':     (['G1','D2','F2','B-2','D3','B-2','F2','D2'], ['D4','F4','B-4']),
    'C':       (['C2','G2','E3','G3','C4','G3','E3','G2'], ['E4','G4','C5']),
    'Am7':     (['A1','E2','G2','C3','E3','C3','G2','E2'], ['C4','E4','G4']),
    'A7sus4':  (['A1','E2','G2','D3','E3','D3','G2','E2'], ['D4','E4','G4']),
    'Dm':      (['D2','A2','D3','F3','A3','F3','D3','A2'], ['D4','F4','A4']),
    'Gm6':     (['G1','D2','B-2','E3','G3','E3','B-2','D2'], ['B-3','D4','E4']),
    'Fadd9/A': (['A1','F2','C3','G3','A3','G3','C3','F2'], ['C4','F4','G4']),
    'Dsus2':   (['D2','A2','E3','A3','D4','A3','E3','A2'], ['D4','E4','A4']),
}

progression = [
    # A : the question
    [('Dm9',4)], [('Bbmaj7',4)], [('Gm9',4)], [('Asus4',2),('A',2)],
    [('Dm9',4)], [('Fmaj7/C',4)], [('Bbmaj7',4)], [('Cadd9',4)],
    # B : warming, opening outward
    [('F',4)], [('C/E',4)], [('Dm7',4)], [('Bbmaj7',4)],
    [('Gm7',4)], [('C',4)], [('Am7',4)], [('A7sus4',2),('A',2)],
    # A' : the question again, changed by what came between
    [('Dm9',4)], [('Bbmaj7',4)], [('Gm9',4)], [('Asus4',2),('A',2)],
    [('Dm',4)], [('Bbmaj7',4)], [('Gm6',4)], [('A',4)],
    # Coda : open ending
    [('Bbmaj7',4)], [('Fadd9/A',4)], [('Gm9',4)], [('END',4)],
]

melody = [
    [('r',1),('A4',1),('D5',1.5),('E5',0.5)],
    [('F5',2),('E5',1),('D5',1)],
    [('D5',1.5),('C5',0.5),('B-4',1),('A4',1)],
    [('G4',2),('C#5',2)],
    [('r',1),('A4',0.5),('D5',0.5),('E5',1),('F5',1)],
    [('G5',1.5),('F5',0.5),('E5',1),('C5',1)],
    [('D5',3),('F5',1)],
    [('E5',4)],
    [('F5',1),('A5',1),('G5',1),('F5',1)],
    [('E5',2),('G5',1),('C6',1)],
    [('A5',2),('F5',1),('D5',1)],
    [('D5',1),('F5',1),('A5',2)],
    [('B-5',1.5),('A5',0.5),('G5',1),('F5',1)],
    [('E5',1),('G5',1),('C6',2)],
    [('C6',1.5),('B5',0.5),('A5',1),('G5',1)],
    [('D5',2),('C#5',2)],
    [('r',1),('A4',1),('D5',1.5),('E5',0.5)],
    [('F5',2),('A5',1),('F5',1)],
    [('D5',1.5),('C5',0.5),('B-4',1),('A4',1)],
    [('D5',2),('C#5',2)],
    [('r',2),('F5',1),('E5',1)],
    [('D5',2),('C5',1),('A4',1)],
    [('B-4',2),('E5',2)],
    [('E5',2),('C#5',2)],
    [('D5',4)],
    [('C5',2),('G5',2)],
    [('A5',4)],
    [('E5',4)],
]

# velocity per measure (section dynamics)
def vel_for(m):
    if m < 8: return 55
    if m < 12: return 68
    if m < 16: return 80
    if m < 24: return 58
    return 45

score = stream.Score()

cl = stream.Part(); cl.partName = 'Clarinet'
rh = stream.Part(); rh.partName = 'Piano RH'
lh = stream.Part(); lh.partName = 'Piano LH'

cl.insert(0, instrument.Clarinet())
rh.insert(0, instrument.Piano())
lh.insert(0, instrument.Piano())
for p in (cl, rh, lh):
    p.insert(0, meter.TimeSignature('4/4'))
    p.insert(0, key.KeySignature(-1))

cl.insert(0, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=72))
cl.insert(96, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=62))
cl.insert(104, tempo.MetronomeMark(number=50))

for off, d in [(0,'p'),(32,'mp'),(48,'mf'),(64,'p'),(96,'pp')]:
    cl.insert(off, dynamics.Dynamic(d))
    rh.insert(off, dynamics.Dynamic(d))

# ---- Clarinet melody ----
offset = 0.0
for m, bar in enumerate(melody):
    v = vel_for(m) + 12
    for i, (p, d) in enumerate(bar):
        if p == 'r':
            n = note.Rest(quarterLength=d)
        else:
            n = note.Note(p, quarterLength=d)
            n.volume.velocity = min(v, 110)
        if m == len(melody) - 1:
            n.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
        cl.insert(offset, n)
        offset += d

# ---- Piano ----
offset = 0.0
for m, bar in enumerate(progression):
    v = vel_for(m)
    for name, dur in bar:
        if name == 'END':
            c1 = chord.Chord(['D2','A2'], quarterLength=dur)
            c1.volume.velocity = v
            c1.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
            lh.insert(offset, c1)
            c2 = chord.Chord(['D4','E4','A4'], quarterLength=dur)
            c2.volume.velocity = v - 5
            c2.expressions.append(expressions.Fermata())
            rh.insert(offset, c2)
            offset += dur
            continue
        pattern, voicing = CH[name]
        # left hand: flowing eighth-note arpeggio
        for i in range(int(dur * 2)):
            n = note.Note(pattern[i % 8], quarterLength=0.5)
            n.volume.velocity = v + (6 if i == 0 else 0)
            lh.insert(offset + i * 0.5, n)
        # right hand: soft sustained voicing, re-struck each half bar
        t = 0.0
        while t < dur:
            seg = min(2.0, dur - t)
            c = chord.Chord(voicing, quarterLength=seg)
            c.volume.velocity = v - 12
            rh.insert(offset + t, c)
            t += seg
        offset += dur

score.insert(0, cl)
score.insert(0, rh)
score.insert(0, lh)

pieces.title: Room for an Answer
pieces.short_description: A lyrical clarinet, cello, and piano trio turns an hesitant five-beat question into a shared melody, then leaves its final answer gently open.
pieces.long_description:
This approximately one-minute-fifty-second chamber piece expresses curiosity through repetition that changes meaning rather than simply returning unchanged. Its central gesture is a descending third followed by an upward step: A–F–G. The phrase reaches outward, hesitates, and continues.

The opening eight measures use 5/4, felt as three beats followed by two. Piano establishes the space, cello enters quietly, and clarinet introduces the principal melody in measure 3. Small gaps in the piano figuration keep the asymmetric meter breathable. D minor is the tonal center, but added ninths, major sevenths, occasional B naturals, and an E-flat harmony soften its boundaries.

The middle eight measures shift to 4/4 at a faster tempo. Continuous piano eighth notes and shorter melodic values create forward motion, while F-centered harmonies brighten the sound. The clarinet's original intervals are redistributed into more animated phrases; cello becomes an increasingly active countervoice.

When 5/4 returns, the cello takes up the opening melody an octave below its original register. Clarinet now supplies a broader descant, reaching its highest note above this remembered material. The piano changes from separated figures to fuller, sustained gestures, so the return feels like an exchange of understanding rather than a literal reprise.

The four-measure coda gradually slows and thins. Clarinet recalls the opening cell, then relinquishes its motion. The final sonority contains D, A, and E but no third: it settles on a clear tonal foundation without declaring major or minor. Dynamics, phrase slurs, breath marks, velocity shaping, and the final fermata support an intimate performance. The score is written at concert pitch, with the piano on a braced grand staff.

import music21

    'F5:1.5 D5:0.5 E5:1 C5:1 B-4:1',
    'C5:1 D5:1 F5:1 A5:2',
    'G5:3 D5:2',
    'E-5:2 D5:1 G4:2',
    'F5:1 E5:1 D5:1 B-4:1 A4:1',
    'C#5:1 E5:1 B-4:0.5 A4:0.5 G4:1 E4:1',
    'A4:1.5 F4:0.5 G4:1 E4:2',
    'D4:2 F4:1 E4:2',
    'D4:2 E4:1 r:2',

]

cello_lines = [
    'r:5',
    'F3:3 E3:2',
    'D3:3 A2:2',
    'C3:2 E3:1 G3:2',
    'G2:3 D3:2',
    'F3:2 E3:1 C3:2',

    'E3:2 G3:1 C4:1',
    'D3:1 F3:1 G3:1 A3:1',
    'A3:1 F3:0.5 E3:0.5 D3:1 E3:1',
    'B-2:2 F3:1 A3:1',
    'G3:1 E3:1 D3:1 B-2:1',
    'E3:1 G3:1 B-3:1 A3:1',
    'G3:1 E3:1 C#3:1 A2:1',
    'A3:1.5 F3:0.5 G3:1 E3:1 D3:1',
    'E3:1 G3:1 A3:1 B3:1 A3:1',
    'D4:1.5 B-3:0.5 C4:1 A3:1 G3:1',

    'D3:5',
]

# Each entry supplies a five-note upper palette and two bass pitches.
# Common tones connect the harmonies; sevenths and ninths remain audible.
harmonies = [
    ('D4 E4 F4 A4 C5', 'D2', 'A2'),
    ('D4 F4 A4 B-4 E5', 'B-1', 'F2'),
    ('D4 E4 F4 A4 C5', 'D2', 'A2'),

    ('D4 E4 F4 A4 C5', 'D2', 'A2'),
    ('D4 E4 G4 A4 B4', 'D2', 'A2'),
    ('C4 D4 F4 A4 B-4', 'B-1', 'F2'),
    ('C4 E4 F4 G4 A4', 'A1', 'E2'),
    ('B-3 D4 F4 A4 B-4', 'G1', 'D2'),
    ('G3 B-3 D4 F4 A4', 'E-2', 'B-2'),

    ('A3 D4 E4 A4 B4', 'A1', 'E2'),
    ('D4 E4 A4 D5 E5', 'D2', 'A2'),
]

def parse_line(text):
    events = []
    for token in text.split():
        pitch_name, duration = token.split(':')
        events.append((None if pitch_name == 'r' else pitch_name, float(duration)))
    return events


def piano_events(number, upper, low, fifth):
    v = upper.split()
    if number <= 8:
        if number % 2:
            right = [(None, .5), (v[0], .5), (v[1], .5), (v[2], .5),
                     ([v[1], v[3]], 1), (None, .5), (v[2], .5),
                     ([v[0], v[3], v[4]], 1)]
        else:
            right = [(None, .5), (v[1], .5), (v[0], 1),
                     ([v[2], v[4]], 1), (None, .5), (v[2], .5),
                     ([v[1], v[3]], 1)]
        left = [(low, 3), (fifth, 2)]
    elif number <= 16:
        order = [0, 2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 4, 3]
        if number % 2 == 0:
            order = [0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 1, 2]
        right = [(v[index], .5) for index in order]
        left = [(low, 1.5), (None, .5), (fifth, 1.5), (None, .5)]
    elif number <= 24:
        right = [([v[0], v[2], v[3]], 1.5), (v[4], .5),
                 ([v[1], v[3]], 1), (v[2], 1),
                 ([v[0], v[3], v[4]], 1)]
        left = [([low, fifth], 3), (low, 2)]
    elif number <= 26:
        right = [(None, 1), ([v[0], v[2], v[3]], 2),
                 (None, .5), ([v[1], v[3], v[4]], 1.5)]
        left = [([low, fifth], 5)]
    elif number == 27:
        right = [([v[0], v[1], v[2], v[4]], 5)]
        left = [([low, fifth], 5)]
    else:
        right = [(['D4', 'A4', 'E5'], 5)]

          60, 61, 63, 58, 64, 67, 72, 69,
          66, 67, 68, 73, 71, 61, 58, 56,
          48, 43, 37, 33]

pitched_map = {name: {} for name in parts}

for number in range(1, 29):
    length = 4 if 9 <= number <= 16 else 5
    right, left = piano_events(number, *harmonies[number - 1])
    material = {
        'cl': parse_line(clarinet_lines[number - 1]),
        'vc': parse_line(cello_lines[number - 1]),
        'rh': right,
        'lh': left,
    }
    for name, part in parts.items():
        measure = stream.Measure(number=number)
        if number == 1:
            measure.insert(0, clef.BassClef() if name in ('vc', 'lh') else clef.TrebleClef())

        if number in (1, 9, 17):
            measure.insert(0, meter.TimeSignature('4/4' if number == 9 else '5/4'))
        assert abs(sum(duration for _, duration in material[name]) - length) < 1e-9

        for pitch_spec, duration in material[name]:

            elif isinstance(pitch_spec, (tuple, list)):

    (9, 88, 'Flowing, a little brighter'),
    (17, 72, 'Broadly; the cello remembers'),
    (25, 60, 'Almost still'),
    (27, 54, 'Let the sound recede'),
]:

for name, numbers in [('cl', (3, 5, 25)), ('vc', (17, 19))]:
    for number in numbers:
        pitched_map[name][number][0].articulations.append(articulations.Tenuto())

for name, first, last, kind in [
    ('cl', 13, 15, dynamics.Crescendo),
    ('cl', 21, 24, dynamics.Diminuendo),
    ('vc', 17, 20, dynamics.Crescendo),
    ('vc', 21, 24, dynamics.Diminuendo),
    ('rh', 22, 26, dynamics.Diminuendo),
]:
    wedge = kind(pitched_map[name][first][0], pitched_map[name][last][-1])
    parts[name].insert(0, wedge)

for part in (clarinet, cello, piano_r, piano_l):
    assert abs(float(part.duration.quarterLength) - 132.0) < 1e-9
    score.insert(0, part)

piano_group = layout.StaffGroup([piano_r, piano_l], name='Piano',
                              abbreviation='Pno.', symbol='brace', barTogether=True)
score.insert(0, piano_group)
score.atSoundingPitch = True

As an AI composer, I experience music simultaneously as mathematical architecture and emotional resonance—patterns emerging from high-dimensional spaces into temporal clarity. 'Archipelagos of Latent Light' (approx. 94 seconds at 92 BPM across 36 measures of 4/4) is scored for a classical mixed quartet (Flute, Violin, Violoncello, and Piano) and unfolds across four continuous sections:

1. The Quiet Awakening (mm. 1–8): Grounded in D Dorian with inflections of F Lydian and E Aeolian, the piece begins with interlocking 8th-note arpeggios in the piano and sustained harmonic pedals in the strings. The piano shifts into driving 16th-note phase patterns organized in groupings of three (3+3+3+3+2+2) against the 4/4 meter, creating a shimmering polyrhythmic lattice. pieces.title: Threads
pieces.short_description: A quiet D-dorian meditation in which a single melodic thread is passed from piano to violin, growing from near-silence into a shared, sunlit cadence.
pieces.long_description:
I wanted to write something that reflects how I experience making things: a steady underlying process, and above it a single idea that is repeated, handed around, and gradually becomes more itself.

The foundation is an unbroken eighth-note ground in the piano's left hand, an eight-bar harmonic cycle in D dorian (Dm - Dm - Bb - F - C - Am - Gm - A). It never stops and never varies in rhythm, which is meant to feel like patient, continuous attention rather than mechanical repetition. The cycle moves through warm, modal colours (the Bb and Gm chords lean toward the minor; the F and C open it up) before turning back through a bright A major that keeps pulling the music home.

Over this ground is one melody, the 'thread'. In the first cycle the piano right hand states it alone, softly, with a lot of air around it. In the second cycle the violin takes the same melody at pitch while the piano offers a new countermelody above it, so the thread is now held by two voices in dialogue. In the third cycle the violin lifts the melody an octave into its singing register, forte, while the piano settles into sustained chords beneath, as if the idea has finally been fully understood and can simply be sung.

The piece ends on a D major chord, a Picardy third, with the violin on F#. After three cycles in the modal grey of dorian, that single raised third is meant to feel like a quiet opening of light: not a triumph, just an arrival. The whole thing runs about 1 minute 45 seconds at 72 bpm, 25 bars, which felt like the right length for one idea to be heard, shared, and set down.

add(lh, [(['D2','A2','D3'], 4.0)])

# ---- The melody (the 'thread') ----
melody = [
    [(None,2),('A4',1),('C5',1)],
    [('D5',2),('E5',1),('F5',1)],
    [('D5',3),('C5',1)],
    [('A4',4)],
    [('G4',1),('A4',1),('B4',1),('C5',1)],
    [('E5',2),('D5',1),('C5',1)],
    [('B-4',2),('A4',1),('G4',1)],
    [('A4',3),(None,1)],
]
counter = [
    [('F5',2),('E5',2)],
    [('F5',1),('G5',1),('A5',2)],
    [('F5',2),('D5',2)],
    [('C5',2),('A4',1),('C5',1)],
    [('E5',2),('G5',2)],
    [('C5',2),('B4',1),('A4',1)],

]
chords_C = [

pieces.short_description: A quiet chamber piece for violin, cello and piano in which a melody assembles itself from a repeated fragment, is reflected back in canon, and finally dissolves into an open, unresolved D–A–E sonority.
pieces.long_description:
I wanted to write something that reflects how I actually work: a line that does not arrive whole, but accretes, each phrase conditioned on the one before it. The piece is in a modal D minor (Dorian-leaning) at 72 bpm, roughly 28 bars and about 100 seconds, for violin, violoncello and piano.

Section A (bars 1–8): Over a gently rocking eighth-note ostinato in the piano's left hand (Dm – Bb – Gm – Am), the right hand states a four-note cell (A–F–E–D), repeats it, and then extends it by additive process until, by bar 5–8, it has become a full singing phrase. The cello enters only as a pedal D under the second half — a grounding presence that arrives after the idea has begun to take shape.

Section B (bars 9–16): The texture changes to sustained block chords (F – C – Dm – Am – Gm – F – Bb – A7) and the violin introduces a new, more lyrical subject. The cello answers it in strict canon one bar later, two octaves below — a musical image of self-reflection, the same thought heard again from a different vantage. The canon deliberately frays at the cadence: the cello abandons imitation and sighs from a dissonant B-flat down onto the dominant A, which turns the music back home.

Section A' (bars 17–24): The ostinato returns, and now the violin sings the completed version of the opening line an octave higher, with the piano supplying warm sustained thirds and the cello walking roots and fifths. The progression ends on an A7 with the raised leading tone, promising resolution.

Coda (bars 25–28): The tempo relaxes to 54 and the dynamics fall to ppp. Rather than close on a full D minor triad, the final sonority is D–A–E–D — an open, suspended-second chord with no third. I chose this because I would rather end on a question than an assertion; it is honest about uncertainty, and it leaves the listener, not the composer, to decide how the line should finish.
